proposal.utterance: What BFO category best fits 'the normative force of an obligation'?

entities.label: NormativeForce
entities.rationale: Normative force is the capacity of an obligation to bind its bearer — to compel or orient action. It is internally grounded in the obligation itself (qua norm or role-bearing entity), not merely an externally assigned label. BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016) captures precisely this: a realizable entity that is grounded in the intrinsic structure of its bearer and can be realized in processes of compliance, enforcement, or acknowledgment. It is not a Quality (which would be a measurable, non-realizable property), not a Role (which is externally grounded), and not a Process (which is an occurrent). The normative force is something the obligation has by virtue of what it is, and it is realized in acts of compliance or enforcement.

relations.rationale: NormativeForce is a subclass of Disposition, as it is an internally grounded realizable entity inhering in an obligation-bearing entity.
Disposition is itself a subclass of Realizable Entity (BFO_0000017); this chain is implicit but worth noting for reasoner traversal.

open_questions: Should NormativeForce be modeled as a subclass of the existing working:LegalObligation's associated disposition, or as a standalone disposition class applicable to any norm?
Do you wish to assert that instances of NormativeForce are realized in processes of type working:BehavioralLegalManifestation (compliance acts), or a new class of enforcement/compliance process?

Is 'normative force' here specifically legal normative force (inhering in legal obligations), or does it apply to moral obligations as well? This affects whether it should be a subclass of a more specific obligation-linked disposition or remain general.
Should working:LegalObligation (currently typed as BFO_0000023 Role and BFO_0000020 SDC) be the canonical bearer class for NormativeForce instances, given that obligations already inhere in persons?
proposal.rationale_summary: The normative force of an obligation is best captured as a BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016). A disposition is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a bearer and is grounded in that bearer's intrinsic structure — it need not be exercised at any given moment but can be realized in processes. Normative force fits this profile: it is the binding capacity that an obligation carries by virtue of being an obligation, realized in processes such as compliance, enforcement, or adjudication. It is not a Quality (BFO_0000019), which would be a non-realizable measurable property. It is not a Role (BFO_0000023), which is externally conferred. It is not a Process (BFO_0000015), which is an occurrent unfolding in time. The existing working:LegalObligation class is already typed as a Role/SDC; NormativeForce would be a distinct disposition that inheres in whatever entity bears the obligation (a person, institution, or legal system), realized when that entity acts in conformity with or is compelled by the norm. A new class working:NormativeForce as a subclass of BFO_0000016 is proposed.
